Since the metric store has no memory data before 3/20, the only remaining way to establish whether the cycle is new is the historical incident/deployment record. A pre-existing restart cadence on this service would demote H1's origin claim.

critiques.summary: H1 is the best-supported origin and no competing hypothesis names a different origin that the evidence cannot separate. Verified grounding: (1) shape — gradual monotonic ~48%→98% heap ramp over ~22h, resetting on restart, across three cycles (F9,F15,F19), which contradicts the replay/burst narrative; (2) onset — growth begins at the dep-5402 activation boundary (F15) after a flat, reset-free baseline with exactly zero restarts before 3/21T22:59:50Z (F27,F28,F29,F30); (3) ordering — 20-min lag zooms show lag FOLLOWS the OOM, not precedes it (F10,F17), and the co-consumer settlement-service on the same shared broker stays flat (F18), ruling out broker-wide replay; (4) timing — memory was already ~88% at 16:00Z and rose through the 18:00Z cfg-2410 change, so the maintenance did not inflect growth (F14,F13). H2/H4 are rejected on verified contradictions (pre-existing cycle, change shape, flat co-consumer, non-shared node), not on assumption; H3 is correctly a corollary of H1. The one genuinely unverified hop is H1's internal mechanism — that the TemplateCache is unbounded (F16 size=188100/evictions=0 cannot distinguish unbounded growth from a bounded no-eviction high-water mark) — and this is now confirmed permanently unobtainable: the dep-5402 implementation/diff is not retrievable, no cache-size config exists, and no cache_size metric is exposed (F41). Critically, H5 does NOT name a different origin: it keeps dep-5402 as the trigger and differs only on the internal allocation path, so the fix direction (revert/patch dep-5402) is unchanged. That makes the residual uncertainty a secondary-mechanism/calibration matter rather than a genuine hypothesis fork, so 'inconclusive' is not warranted. Remaining limitations to carry as calibration and assumptions: the pre-deploy baseline is only ~1 day (3/20) and pre-3/21 telemetry/record is simply absent (F26,F31,F36), so 'the ~23h cycle did not exist before dep-5402' is established for 3/20 onward only, not the full requested window; the 3/23 20-min lag ordering rests on 2h buckets (its fine-grained query 503'd), though the ordering proof holds for 3/21 for the identical restart signature. No blocking issue remains that obtainable evidence could resolve.

challenges.issue: The load-bearing mechanism — the TemplateCache being effectively unbounded — is inference from absence-of-mention (F20,F21,F22,F23) plus a single sample (F16 size=188100/evictions=0). This cannot distinguish unbounded growth from a bounded no-eviction high-water mark over a finite key space (templates x locales x segments, cardinality never obtained, F24/F42). This is now confirmed permanently unobtainable (no diff/source, no cache_size metric, F41) so it is a calibration limit rather than a blocking gap.

The 'no pre-existing cycle' claim rests on a ~1-day pre-deploy baseline (3/20 flat, F27) plus zero restarts back to 3/20 (F28,F29,F30); memory_pct and the deployment/ticket record are simply absent before 2026-03-20T00:00Z / 2026-03-21 (F26,F31,F36), so a prior cycle in 3/10–3/19 cannot be positively excluded. Bounded by permanent data unavailability, so it lowers confidence rather than invalidating the origin.

H3 is labeled 'active' at 0.50 but names no independent origin — it is an ordering corollary of H1, and its 3/23 lag-vs-OOM ordering rests on 2h buckets because the 20-min zoom 503'd (the ordering proof comes from the 3/21 restart). Its confidence is inflated relative to its role; it should not be read as a competing causal hypothesis.

H5 cites F16 as contradicting, but the 188100/evictions=0 sample does not actually contradict H5 — a bounded key space at high-water mark with no evictions would produce the same reading. H5 remains live as an internal-mechanism alternative, but it does not name a different origin (it retains dep-5402 as trigger), so it does not force an inconclusive verdict.
